# `scripts/post-process/halo_table_io.py`

Source: [halo_table_io.py](../../../../scripts/post-process/halo_table_io.py)

```text
halo_table_io.py: the value-added halo tables out_<snap>.vahc, .tens and .vpot (vahc_fast.py), as text or binary.

Text (as before): '#' header lines (line 2 = column names), then one row per halo, values space separated.
Binary (same file name): the same '#' header lines, then one line
    #SAHYADRI-BINARY v1 rows=<n> dtype=<JSON list of [name, numpy type]>
and the rows as packed little-endian records (numpy structured array, tobytes()). Values are those the text
would hold: the text writes str() of the same float32/int64 numbers (the shortest string that reads back to the
same float32), so the FITS tables made from either are identical.

  write(path, arr, header, binary=True)   via <path>.part and rename (a killed job leaves no complete-looking file)
  header_lines(path)       the '#' lines before the data (without the #SAHYADRI-BINARY line)
  names(path)              column names (header line 2)
  is_binary(path)
  read(path)               float64 array (rows, columns), as np.loadtxt(path, ndmin=2)
  read_records(path)       structured array (binary: memory map; text: parsed with the header names)
  iter_chunks(path, chunk) float64 arrays of <= chunk rows, in order
  column(path, name)       one column (binary: without reading the others)
```

## Contents

- [`_scan`](#_scan) - (header lines as str, binary info dict or None, data offset in bytes).
- [`header_lines`](#header_lines) - The `#` header lines of a halo table (text or binary).
- [`names`](#names) - Column names from the second header line.
- [`is_binary`](#is_binary) - True if the table is in the binary format (header line with row count and dtype).
- [`_memmap`](#_memmap) - Memory map of the rows of a binary table, or None for a text table; raises ValueError if the file is shorter than its header says.
- [`_to_float`](#_to_float) - Structured array -&gt; 2-D float64 array (one column per field).
- [`read`](#read) - The whole table as a 2-D float64 array (text: `np.loadtxt`; binary: memory map).
- [`read_records`](#read_records) - The whole table as a structured array with the column names (binary: the memory map itself).
- [`iter_chunks`](#iter_chunks) - Yield the table as 2-D float64 arrays of at most `chunk` rows.
- [`column`](#column) - One column by name as a 1-D array (binary: from the memory map; text: read with pandas).
- [`write`](#write) - header: the '#' lines (one string, each line ending in '\n'; line 2 = column names, as many as arr has fields). Text rows: str() of every value, as AddValue wrote them, formatted step rows at a time (bounded memory). Binary: the records under the header names, little endian.
